gloss: Every Map address, grouped by tab, with what it holds.
narrative: Reads docs/map-tabs.csv, one row per address, and the TABS and SUBVIEWS arrays in lib/alpineComponents/map.js, which say which tab holds each address and in what order. Each row shows the address's sentence, the same one its Sources and methods opens with, and opens the address. The finder matches a row's name, its tab and its sentence, and also the files the row names: the paths its sentence links and those its narrative cites, which it then lists under the sentence. A bare ?view=map lands here.

gloss: Repositories and outposts the hub reaches, joined by delivery route.
narrative: Reads docs/portable.csv and counts its rows by the use column; each count is one edge from the hub to the set, labeled with the route and the count, and selecting an edge opens those rows in Distribution. The set is the hub's own .web-tools.json and, with a token, every estate repository in the crawled config cache, each styled by its GitHub visibility. Outposts come from docs/outposts.csv, each joined to the repository its declared column names; a repository an outpost names that no manifest supplies is drawn as named but not read.

gloss: Artifacts selected to travel, by delivery route.
narrative: Reads docs/portable.csv. Each row names its kind (skill, document, directory, or standalone tool) and links to the Skills, Docs, or Automation inventory that owns it. A row's title opens the file in the swipe deck the Docs tab uses; a directory row opens its folder, and every row's GitHub icon opens the source peek. The tab carries its own search box.

gloss: Primitives that make a session's work visible in chat.
narrative: Reads docs/surfacing.csv, which indexes the primitives of docs/SURFACING.md. Sources and methods lists the document's related regions and their delivery rules. The header's Read control opens the document in the Docs tab's swipe deck, so a docked reader sees the prose beside the cards rather than in place of them.

gloss: Links that show a change, and what each misses.
narrative: Reads docs/showing-mechanisms.csv for the mechanisms and what each misses, then docs/routes.json for the address grammar, docs/routes-modes.csv for toss-render's delivery modes and their trust postures, and docs/routes-routes.csv for the toss routes. The rule for picking a mechanism is executable rather than written here: npm run showing reads a branch's changed files and prints the link that reaches them.

gloss: Documents in each estate repository, by folder.
narrative: A strip picks the repository. For web-tools, reads docs/docs.csv: each document's subject, status, reach, words with their share of the folder, and maintenance behind one toggle. For every other repository, reads state/docs.json in the private registry, the hourly crawl's index of each Markdown file with its word count (lib/kits/doc-index.js), shown only with a token; those rows have no subject, status or reach. Both carry readership, the distinct sessions that opened the file, from the sessions cache. A folder rail rolls up counts and words. A row's title opens the document in a fullscreen swipe deck over its folder; the GitHub icon opens the source peek.

gloss: The estate's mission, its five goals, and reading paths.
narrative: Renders docs/aims.json, which holds the mission sentence, with docs/aims-goals.csv for the goals and docs/aims-reading.csv for the ordered reading paths. The paths begin with the repository README, the agent contract, and the docs index. Addressed as ?tab=aims, its key from when it was a top-level tab.

gloss: Document lengths across the repository's history.
refs: Document lengths across the repository's history=data/doc-growth/
narrative: Charts the doc-growth payload (data/doc-growth/*.json) of every repository that declares a growth path in its .web-tools.json, the hub included. The hub's payload is a public fetch, so the chart renders without a token; the selector between repositories needs one.

gloss: Prose repeated across files, identically or in similar wording.
narrative: Reads docs/themes.csv, the pairs of Markdown files that share runs of ten identical words, and data/doc-overlap/, passage embeddings measured by hand. One list holds both: the groups of files a repeat connects, heaviest first, at the threshold the slider sets, then the pairs similar only in wording, from cosine 0.78 with passages of 20 words or more. A card per row maps where each repeat sits in each file, as ribbons, bars or a dot plot, then shows the runs in the file's own text and the similar passages side by side with each file's share, less those a run already shows. A rule repeated in files that all leave this repo is marked to review.

gloss: Executables the repository runs on itself, by trigger.
narrative: Reads docs/harness.csv: an authored role per file, plus derived layer, line count, invocation route, what runs it, whether the file writes files, whether prose names it, and whether a test exercises it. The row above the files says what starts a thing running: Event and Schedule open views of their own (?tab=events and ?tab=scheduled), and On demand and No route filter the files. A file counts under each trigger that reaches it, through its own route or through what runs it. A folder rail mirrors the tree on disk with counts and blank roles rolled up, re-weighted by the pick. The commit hook's row counts its steps, listed under Events, from docs/hook-legs.csv.

gloss: Ongoing concerns, with what each governs and measures.
narrative: Reads each estate repository's programs declaration in .web-tools.json: the hub at the selected revision, the others from the private registry's config cache with a token. One row per program: its charter, the files it governs (opened under the row), its open tasks (rows of the declaring repository's board.csv whose project is the program's name), its measures, the reviewer agents from docs/agents.csv, and the app views that display it. Each program's folder holds its charter as README.md; the programs skill and the program-files hook read the same declaration.

gloss: What runs when an event happens, by kind of event.
narrative: One section per kind of event, in the order a change meets them: the environment build, the Claude Code session, git, then GitHub Actions. Claude Code's section reads docs/hook-events.csv, every event the installed Claude Code accepts a hook on with its /hooks summary, and skills/hooks/hooks.json, the plugin's registrations, in columns by phase; an event with no hook stays, dimmed. The other kinds group docs/harness.csv's event-fired files by the event their route names, and the commit hook's steps from docs/hook-legs.csv are listed open under pre-commit. Opened from the Automation tab's Event trigger.

gloss: Tasks the estate runs on a schedule, with their stages.
narrative: Reads web-tools-private's data/design/scheduled-tasks.csv and scheduled-task-stages.csv with a token, as Context reads its private half, and state/scheduled-tasks.json when a task has run. The registry's schedule column, cron in UTC, is the only place a task's timing is set: scheduled-tasks.yml runs hourly and starts what is due. Each card states its schedule in words and its next firing in local time, the events that also start its workflow and the inputs the scheduled-tasks workflow passes, read from the workflow file, and its last run, from the state file or the Actions API. A workflow that still carries its own cron is flagged. A task run inside the scheduled-tasks workflow shows its stage ladder with how many targets reached each stage.

gloss: What sets state in the estate, by where it runs.
refs: What sets state in the estate=docs/writers.csv;where it runs=docs/venues.md
narrative: Reads docs/writers.csv, one row per writer, and docs/direct-to-main.csv for the paths each one sets on main. Three columns: what starts a writer; the writers, boxed by the machine they run on, an agent carrying its model; and where what they set lands. Lines join a start to its writers and a writer to where it sets. A dotted loop joins a writer to one it starts, dashed where that one polls. Hovering or picking a box lights what it connects to. A picked writer's card says the same in words, adds how it sets, the paths it sets on main, and how its commits read in the Writes view. On a phone the lines drop and the card carries them.

gloss: Checks, what they protect, and how they run.
narrative: Reads each repository's checking.execution declarations for purpose and limits, and the referenced workflow job and step for commands, runners, triggers and conditions. Results link to GitHub without claiming a status for the selected revision. Web Tools owns the shared view; each repository owns its descriptions, and the private registry supplies discovery through its derived config cache. Below, docs/tests.csv supplies the hub's individual check inventory and the dated checking readings retain their original dates. Counts measure named test declarations, not individual assertions or pass results; loops can produce more cases when run. Kind and protects are authored; method, runner and startup-only test counts are derived from the files. Browser checks use their own harnesses and have no comparable test count.

gloss: How instructions and automation shape a session.
refs: How instructions and automation shape a session=docs/context-sources.csv
narrative: Questions and sources in one workspace. The questions list above one source table; picking a question filters the table and shows its relationship and declared paths, and picking it again or Show all lists every source. A source's details open in a panel-tip on hover or a click: each classified property drawn as its whole scale with the source's value lit, the meanings from docs/vocabularies.csv, its connections and its questions. Usage sorting distinguishes startup presence from skill invocation, and unavailable measurements from zero. Session records retains unclaimed files and skills. Data comes from docs/context-sources.csv, the optional private registry, docs/context-links.csv and skills/hooks/hooks.json. ctxsort, ctxtopic and ctxsource preserve order, question and the pinned source; the retired ctxlens lands on the whole table.

gloss: Events, and what each one does to a session's layers.
narrative: Reads docs/environment/lifetimes.json, whose facts belong to docs/environment/container.md. Each event row carries a dot per layer coloured by its effect, so the list is the whole effect table. A pick redraws the detail: a worked week that lights the marks the event owns, the event's trigger and sources, then one row per layer with its lifetime on a ruler, its effect, and its items. An item the event affects is a pill ending in a badge that names what happens; the rest follow, dimmed. An item's icon says how it arrives: stored on GitHub, set by you, copied in, script output, or made in the session. Two marks flag edits that do not stick and output saved elsewhere.

gloss: Browser JavaScript modules under lib/kits/*.js, and what loads them.
narrative: Reads docs/kits.csv, which is wholly derived. The namespace and gloss come from each file's header comment; then whether every chain-boot page pays for the kit, whether a demo page exists (opened in-app as an app view), how many files load it, and whether a test names it. The strip filters on those. Three warning states render in the warning tone rather than being hidden: a blank gloss, a blank namespace, and a kit nothing loads.

gloss: Skills a session can reach, and their outside sources.
narrative: One card for every skill under two filters, the set (All, Yours, Estate, Third-party) and the subject, each counting under the other and the search box. Yours joins skills/manifest.csv to docs/portable.csv for the command, with a demo badge where the pages catalog lists one. Estate is the skills other repositories declare, from the crawled config cache, shown only with a token. Third-party is docs/upstream-skills.csv. Subjects come from the roster and the upstream registry; the estate declares none yet and sits under Unsorted. A dashed card is one no session loads, archive/skills/archive.csv closes the list, and each card's GitHub icon peeks its SKILL.md.

gloss: Agents a session can run, and where each is defined.
narrative: Reads docs/agents.csv. Definitions are the Claude Code agent files the plugin ships under skills/agents/, each listed in the marketplace entry and called by its namespaced name; a card shows its model, its tools, and the skills it preloads at startup, which are its backing documentation. In skills are the reader roles a skill spawns through the Agent tool with its prompt written into the skill, grouped under that skill. Estate is every other repository's own agents, declared under agents in its .web-tools.json and read from the crawled config cache, shown only with a token. A segmented control picks the set and the search box narrows all three.

gloss: Corrections the owner has repeated, and in how many sessions.
narrative: Reads skills/peeves/peeves.csv, the list the peeves skill carries and the peeves-critic agent preloads. A row's bar is the number of recorded sessions in which the owner made the correction, scaled to the heaviest peeve in the list; the number is an order of magnitude. Area groups by the kind of work. Where written groups by whether the rule is stated only in this list, in a document a session loads, or in a script or hook that catches a trip. A row opens to its statement, what tripping it looks like and where it is written, and, with a token, to the owner's own words from the private registry's sessions/peeves/evidence.csv, each linking to its session.

gloss: Tracked CSV files each repository declares, with their columns.
narrative: Reads the census file each repository names in its .web-tools.json data.census key: the hub's own data/csv-census.csv, and, with a token, those of estate repositories found in the crawled config cache. Each census lists tracked CSV paths, headers, and physical measurements. A file opens in the Files view, where a CSV renders as a filterable table.

gloss: App addresses, by when their code last changed.
narrative: Joins docs/app-routes.csv to the hub's own history: each route's files are dated by their last commit, and open pull requests touching those files are listed against it. It needs a token, and says so without one. The census line counts routes, routes with no file of their own, and routes with work open. The former address ?view=routes forwards here.

gloss: Committed inventories, with what each covers and what checks it.
narrative: Reads docs/registries.csv with docs/properties.csv and docs/vocabularies.csv. One card per registry, grouped by area (files or names), shows its title, gloss, path, gate, target, scope, and a chip per declared property, with totals derived rather than written. Each card lists its renders_in files, the app files that name the registry in code, as peekable links; a registry no app surface reads gets a warning badge and a figure in the strip.

gloss: Rules the documentation settles, by topic, with their source passage.
narrative: Reads docs/policies.csv and docs/policy-topics.csv. A first pass, built 2026-10-01 from a Gemini prototype (web-tools #850) and filled by Haiku readers over the living docs and the governance skills; the suite holds every quoted passage to its document. The rail groups topics under six areas, and the filters split rules by level (principle, policy, standard) and by origin, which is unknown for most rows. The 15 rows carried from the prototype quote session prompts that remain unverified.

gloss: Places outside git that hold estate material, and their upkeep.
narrative: Reads docs/outposts.csv, one card per outpost: its declaration, where its observation comes from and who supplies it, the check that compares them, the upkeep that restores it, and where dated observations are committed. The account card also reads docs/account-skills.csv and, with a token, web-tools-private environment/account-skills.csv, the observation a session last wrote with skills/hooks/account-skills.py --write, listing each skill's state with the ones needing attention first. The live check is that script's session-start hook; the list is only as current as the date it shows.

gloss: UI unit dimensions, their codes, and where each unit falls.
narrative: Reads data/ui-units/: dimensions.csv for the eight dimensions (body, frame, reach, binding, phone, occasion and answer, which readers code against codebook.md, and ring, which node/ui-units.mjs computes), codes.csv for the codes of each, and coded.csv and units.csv for every unit's values. budget-drs units come from home's data/ui-units/ under a token. By dimension, each dimension states what it holds, whether a unit takes one code or any number, and each code's share of the units, opening to its gloss and its units. As a table, one row per unit and one column per dimension, sorted by any column.

gloss: Every coded UI unit's screenshot, its slots outlined and named.
narrative: Reads the same tables as Dimensions, plus thumbs/thumbs.csv for each unit's desktop and phone shot and instances.csv for the pattern a unit's markup declares and whether it held when checked; budget-drs shots come from web-tools-private's thumbs/ under a token, and a link's refs= selection reaches their branches. One section per code of the chosen dimension, each unit a card that opens its section as a deck. Under a body code, the section says which kit draws it and how many units declare it. A warning edge marks a unit whose own code does a job a shared kit already does.

gloss: Projects within each repository, with their trackers, parts and research.
narrative: Reads each estate repository's .web-tools.json: the hub at the selected revision, the others from the private registry's config cache with a token. Each repository is a row of its own, the workspace its root tracker, inbox and research filed under no project belong to, with its declared projects indented under it. Open tasks counts the backlog, in-progress and blocked rows of each tracker's board.csv and draws them as one bar on the fullest board's scale; a board that cannot be read shows a dash. App, Inbox and Outpost mark a project's landing, inbox and powershellOutpost declarations, and Research counts the research accounts whose path falls in the workspace and opens them in Probes or Exploration.

gloss: Probes into our tools, workflows, data, and assumptions.
narrative: Reads research entries marked probe in each repository's manifest. Each entry opens its retained account and the materials linked there. Search and repository filters narrow the accounts; a project association follows the longest declared containing path. Private declarations require the reader's token.

gloss: Information gathered from outside sources.
narrative: Reads research entries marked exploration in the same manifests as Probes. A report remains an account with its sources and findings, rather than a collection of document rows. Missing declarations and failed reads are shown separately from an empty category.

gloss: Paths that let someone else run code on a machine.
narrative: Reads web-tools-private's data/design/triggers.csv with a token, as Scheduled reads its registry. One row per path by which something other than the owner, at the machine, can make it run code: what starts it, who can start it, what else reaches it, what runs and as whom, what limits it, the worst case, and when and how it was checked. Rows are grouped by the machine they reach and open in place; each source links to the file it rests on.

gloss: Every public file, with the patterns worth a look.
narrative: Reads state/watch.json in web-tools-private with a token; sessions/tools/watch_scan.py writes it from this repository's main. Every file is listed with its folder, kind and last commit. A mark is a pattern worth a look, not a finding: another estate repository named, a session link or record id, a chat link, or an email address. A marked file opens to its matching lines, each linking to that line. Images shows every picture, newest first; All lists the folders.

gloss: Email addresses in every checkout, grouped by domain.
narrative: Reads the same scan. Every email address in the checkouts beside the registry, private repositories included, except the addresses tools sign commits with and the reserved example domains. Domains are listed largest first, and each opens to its matches with their file and line.
